summary: Concise editorial opening, preserving the first mystery and withholding visual spoilers.
settingText: EDITORIAL COMPOSITE — Olyria-Prime at shift end and Zenith Spire at night, treated as one elegant symbolic composition rather than a literal shared location. Theo is a small figure at the bottom of a vast black-rock trench under practical work lights. Rae is isolated high in a clean archive plane on the opposite side of the composition. Between them is only darkness, distance and a restrained field of stars; do not show the Desert Marker, any ancient champion, any battlefield, any forbidden name on a screen, or any supernatural memory imagery. Cool steel, charcoal and white light with controlled deep-space color. Reserve broad clean negative space for long editorial copy.

panelPlan.text: Single full-page editorial splash with no gutters. Theo and Rae occupy small opposing anchors in the lower corners; the central and upper field remains visually spacious for the editor copy. The image should promise enormous buried scale while keeping the literal story reveal completely hidden.

directionInline.text: EDITORIAL BOOKEND PAGE — one finished portrait comic/editorial page, not a cover and not a story continuation panel. Use a single integrated full-page composition with strong negative space reserved for the supplied CAPTION text. The illustration must be visually specific to this issue and cinematic, but it must not reveal any story answer, character, champion, object, or event that the issue itself has not yet revealed at this point in the reading order.

Treat every supplied CAPTION line as exact finished lettering. Do not omit, paraphrase, duplicate, reorder, or invent text. Keep the prose effortless to read over the art with deliberate high-contrast text fields and premium prestige-comic editorial typography.

panelPlan.text: Single full-page teaser splash. Make the overlapping but mismatched paper evidence the visual center. Use a dark, clean page with one sharp strip of violet-white reflected light and ample negative space for the teaser copy.

directionInline.text: EDITORIAL BOOKEND PAGE — one finished portrait comic/editorial page, not a cover and not a story continuation panel. Use a single integrated full-page composition with strong negative space reserved for the supplied CAPTION text. The illustration must be visually specific to this issue and cinematic, but it must not reveal any story answer, character, champion, object, or event that the issue itself has not yet revealed at this point in the reading order.

Treat every supplied CAPTION line as exact finished lettering. Do not omit, paraphrase, duplicate, reorder, or invent text. Do not add environmental text, logos, labels, page numbers, credits, or signage beyond the supplied lettering. Keep the prose effortless to read over the art with deliberate high-contrast text fields and premium prestige-comic editorial typography.
